issues.label: Standard of review and role of RAD
Admissibility of new evidence under s.110(4) IRPA
Request for oral hearing under s.110(6) IRPA
Credibility assessment of travel authorization contradiction
Credibility assessment of renunciation of Islam and wearing hijab
Assessment of past persecution allegations and contradictions in testimony
Assessment of text chat evidence and RPD's conclusion on timestamp issue

Final determination on refugee status and protection claim

result.overall: The Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) dismissed the appeal, agreeing with the Refugee Protection Division's (RPD) credibility assessment and finding that the appellants did not meet the burden of proof to establish a risk of persecution or need for protection under IRPA.

themes.name: Standard of review and role of RAD
themes.summary: The RAD must independently assess the evidence but shows deference to the RPD's credibility findings while independently assessing country conditions evidence.

themes.name: Admissibility of new evidence under s.110(4) IRPA
themes.summary: The RAD admitted new evidence submitted by the appellants under section 110(4) but found it did not affect the outcome of the refugee claim.

themes.name: Request for oral hearing under s.110(6) IRPA
themes.summary: The RAD denied the appellants' request for an oral hearing as the new evidence did not justify it.

themes.name: Credibility assessment of travel authorization contradiction
themes.summary: The RAD found a contradiction in the husband's signed travel authorization inconsistent with the claim of his controlling behavior, undermining credibility.

themes.name: Credibility assessment of renunciation of Islam and wearing hijab
themes.summary: The RAD found the appellants' claim of renouncing Islam but wearing hijab to retain parental support lacked credibility given absence of past persecution.

themes.name: Assessment of past persecution allegations and contradictions in testimony
themes.summary: The RAD found contradictions in testimony about an alleged burning incident and concluded it was accidental, not persecution.

themes.name: Assessment of text chat evidence and RPD's conclusion on timestamp issue
themes.summary: The RAD agreed with the RPD that the text chat evidence was not credible due to timestamp inconsistencies and implications of fraud.

themes.name: Risk assessment related to Sharia law and state protection in Lebanon
themes.summary: The RAD found that despite Sharia law issues, the appellants' profile and resources meant they would not face persecution or lack of state protection in Lebanon.

themes.name: Final determination on refugee status and protection claim
themes.summary: The RAD confirmed the RPD's decision that the appellants are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection and dismissed the appeal.

arguments.quote: the RPD did not focus on the important allegations of the Appellants but instead looked for 'minor discrepancies'
arguments.claim: The RPD erred by focusing on minor discrepancies rather than the core allegations of abuse and risk.

arguments.quote: the Principal Appellant has planned this out some time ago and that she had been avoiding a fight with her husband
arguments.claim: The travel authorization signed by the husband is not contradictory because of the appellants' strategic planning and husband's distraction.
arguments.outcome_note: The RAD found the contradiction credible and significant.

arguments.quote: the Principal Appellant's response to the perceive contradiction is plausible within the context of the allegations
arguments.claim: Wearing hijab despite renouncing Islam is plausible to retain parental support and does not undermine credibility.
arguments.outcome_note: The RAD found this explanation insufficient given lack of past persecution evidence.

arguments.quote: there is "no valid reason to doubt the truthfulness of the first Appellant's allegations in regards to the events surrounding the incident as she described..."
arguments.claim: The RPD wrongly interpreted the facts and should have accepted the allegations of abuse as truthful.
arguments.outcome_note: The RAD found contradictions and accepted the RPD's accidental interpretation.

arguments.quote: the Appellants respond to this by provided new evidence which shows that Mr. XXXX was not in America but was in Lebanon
arguments.claim: The RPD erred in disbelieving the text chat evidence because new evidence shows the husband was in Lebanon, not America.
arguments.outcome_note: The RAD found the new evidence did not address the core credibility issue of the timestamp and fraud implication.

arguments.quote: the Appellants argue that these meet the criterial for acceptance under Section 110(4)
arguments.claim: The new evidence submitted meets the criteria for acceptance under s.110(4) IRPA.

arguments.quote: the Appellants seek to be recognized as Convention refugees or persons in need of protection
arguments.claim: The appellants seek recognition as Convention refugees or persons in need of protection or alternatively a re-determination by a different panel.
arguments.outcome_note: The appeal was dismissed and no re-determination ordered.

holdings.quote: I am in agreement with this credibility assessment
holdings.statement: The RAD agrees with the RPD's credibility assessment and confirms the decision rejecting refugee protection claims.

holdings.quote: I must show a degree of deference to the RPD with respect to its credibility assessment
holdings.statement: The RAD must show deference to the RPD's credibility findings but independently assess other evidence such as country conditions.

holdings.quote: this material does meet the legislative test of s. 110(4) for admission and is therefore admitted into evidence before the RAD
holdings.statement: New evidence submitted under s.110(4) IRPA is admitted.

holdings.quote: I am denying the request for an oral hearing under s. 110(6)
holdings.statement: Request for oral hearing is denied as new evidence does not justify it.

holdings.quote: I must conclude that this can be viewed as a contradiction
holdings.statement: The signed travel authorization contradicts the claim of controlling behavior by the husband.

holdings.quote: I must conclude that if Mr. XXXX were really controlling/dominating there would be evidence of an effort to put conditions/restrictions on travel which is not the case
holdings.statement: The absence of travel restrictions undermines the claim of controlling behavior.

holdings.quote: I must conclude that in a situation where the RPD is concluding that the allegations of past persecution lack credibility, the forward looking allegations must also come into question
holdings.statement: Future risk claims based on renunciation of Islam lack credibility if past persecution allegations are not credible.

holdings.quote: there does appear to be an inconsistency
holdings.statement: There is an inconsistency between the Principal Appellant's and witness's testimony about the burning incident.

holdings.quote: I concluded the RPD did not error on this issue
holdings.statement: The RAD agrees with the RPD that the text chat evidence is not credible due to timestamp issues.

holdings.quote: I am in agreement with this conclusion
holdings.statement: The RAD agrees with the RPD that the allegations are embellishments and do not meet the threshold for persecution.

holdings.quote: I must agree with the RPD's conclusion because the Appellants have not shown they have been or will be set apart for treatment consistent with persecution
holdings.statement: The RAD agrees that the appellants would face less than a serious possibility of persecution or risk if returned to Lebanon.

holdings.quote: I confirm the determination of the RPD, namely, that that Ms. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX are neither "Convention refugees" nor "persons in need of protection"
holdings.statement: The RAD confirms the RPD's decision rejecting refugee protection claims.

rebuttals.quote: the RPD did not focus on the important allegations of the Appellants but instead looked for 'minor discrepancies'
rebuttals.point: The RPD focused on minor discrepancies rather than core allegations
rebuttals.court_answer: The RAD found the RPD's focus on discrepancies justified and agreed with the credibility assessment.

rebuttals.quote: the Principal Appellant has planned this out some time ago and that she had been avoiding a fight with her husband
rebuttals.point: The travel authorization is not contradictory due to planning and distraction
rebuttals.court_answer: The RAD concluded the contradiction was credible and undermined the claim of controlling behavior.

rebuttals.quote: the Principal Appellant's response to the perceive contradiction is plausible within the context of the allegations
rebuttals.point: Wearing hijab despite renouncing Islam is plausible
rebuttals.court_answer: The RAD found the explanation insufficient given the lack of credible past persecution evidence.

rebuttals.quote: there is "no valid reason to doubt the truthfulness of the first Appellant's allegations in regards to the events surrounding the incident as she described..."
rebuttals.point: The RPD wrongly doubted the truthfulness of abuse allegations
rebuttals.court_answer: The RAD found contradictions and accepted the RPD's interpretation that the incident was accidental.

rebuttals.quote: the Appellants respond to this by provided new evidence which shows that Mr. XXXX was not in America but was in Lebanon
rebuttals.point: The RPD erred in disbelieving the text chat evidence
rebuttals.court_answer: The RAD found the new evidence did not address the core timestamp issue and sustained the RPD's conclusion of fraud.

authorities.quote: Justice Phelan in Huruglica1 states that the RAD "must review all aspects of the RPD's decision and come to an independent assessment"
authorities.why: Establishes the RAD's role to independently assess evidence with some deference to credibility findings.

authorities.quote: Justice Locke references Huruglica and suggests that "Except in cases where the credibility of a witness is critical or determinative... the RAD must not give any deference"
authorities.why: Clarifies when RAD must defer to RPD credibility findings and when it must independently assess evidence.
